create.statement_tex: For the literal hard-TOP product coefficient C_L(n)=sum_(h|n,h odd,sqrt(n)<=h<=2sqrt(n)) chi_4(h)eta_L(h)Phi(h/(H+1))W(sqrt(q_Xh^2/(4n))), one has sum_n|C_L(n)|^2<<L^2log(2L). If B_L(n)=L^(3/2)n^(-3/4)C_L(n)1_(n nonsquare), then for every squarefree D>1, sum_(sf(n)=D)|B_L(n)|<<_epsilon(1+L/sqrt(D))L^epsilon. The first bound follows from h_1=ga,h_2=gb,m_1=bt,m_2=at; the second from h=gd_1u^2,m=gd_2v^2,d_1d_2=D with sqrt(D)<<A<<L on every nonempty common shell. This is not actual coefficient mass, and the discontinuous divisor-incidence C_L(n) has no proved BV or additive-partial-sum hypothesis authorizing a scalar B-process. Resolving h|n by h^(-1)sum_(a mod h)e(an/h) and setting r=kh-a gives a bijection. The positive saddle is x_(h,r)=Xh^2/(4r^2), with phase Xh/(4r), profile W(r/y), and x^(-3/4)|phi''|^(-1/2)=2J^(-1/2); thus the stationary principal family is 2e(-1/8)L^(3/2)J^(-1/2)sum_(h odd)chi_4(h)eta_L(h)Phi(h/(H+1))/h sum_(J/2<=r<=J)^star W(r/y)e(Xh/(4r)), the original reciprocal hard-TOP principal family. Endpoint, zero, nonstationary, remainder, crossing, and square owners remain separate. Complementary-divisor switching is involutive. Completing C_L=r_2/4-R_L leaves an uncontrolled R_L; importing the desired circle estimate is circular, while an independent radial theorem would still leave R_L. This is a scoped method obstruction, not a lower bound or disproof of hard TOP.
